“Crows pick out the eyes of the dead, when the dead have no longer need of them; but flatterers mar the soul of the living, and her eyes they blind.”
Epictetus
Epictetus is showing us something powerful: crows only harm dead bodies that can’t feel pain anymore. But people who flatter us (those who give us fake praise) are much more dangerous - they hurt our living souls and make us blind to the truth.
When someone always tells us what we want to hear, we stop seeing reality clearly. We become blind to our mistakes and weaknesses. This stops us from growing as people.
The Stoic lesson:
•	Choose honest friends over fake ones
•	Listen to truthful feedback, even when it hurts
•	Don’t let sweet words make you weak
•	Stay awake to reality, not lost in illusions
Real friends tell you the truth. Fake friends tell you what sounds nice.

Turnover is generally faster in younger skin and gradually slows with age.
